knowledge_point.title: Evaluating Surface Integrals Over Parametric Surfaces

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the surface integral

$$
\iint_S f(x,y,z)\,\mathrm{d}S,
$$

where $f(x,y,z)=- x - y$ and

$$
\mathbf r(u,v)=\langle u + 2 v, u - 2 v, v\rangle
$$

for $0\le u\le 3$ and $0\le v\le 2$.

Use the formula

$$
\iint_S f\,\mathrm{d}S=\int_{0}^{2}\int_{0}^{3}f(\mathbf r(u,v))\|\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v\|\,\mathrm{d}u\,\mathrm{d}v.
$$

*Hint: The surface-area factor is $\|\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v\|=3 \sqrt{2}$. First substitute the coordinates into the scalar function and simplify.*
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a scalar surface integral, use

$$
\iint_S f\,\mathrm{d}S=\iint_D f(\mathbf r(u,v))\|\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v\|\,\mathrm{d}A.
$$

The supplied area factor is $3 \sqrt{2}$.

Substitute the coordinates and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}
f(\mathbf r(u,v))&=- \left(u + 2 v\right) - \left(u - 2 v\right) \\
&=- 2 u.
\end{aligned}
$$

Integrate over the parameter rectangle:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\iint_S f\,\mathrm{d}S&=3 \sqrt{2}\int_{0}^{2}\int_{0}^{3}\left(- 2 u\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\,\mathrm{d}v \\
&=3 \sqrt{2}\int_{0}^{2}\left[- u^{2}\right]_{u=0}^{u=3}\,\mathrm{d}v \\
&=3 \sqrt{2}\int_{0}^{2}\left(-9\right)\,\mathrm{d}v \\
&=3 \sqrt{2}\left[- 9 v\right]_{v=0}^{v=2} \\
&=3 \sqrt{2}\left(\left(-18\right)-\left(0\right)\right) \\
&=- 54 \sqrt{2}.
\end{aligned}
$$

knowledge_point.title: Evaluating Surface Integrals Over Parametric Surfaces

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the surface integral

$$
\iint_S f(x,y,z)\,\mathrm{d}S,
$$

where $f(x,y,z)=- x + y$ and

$$
\mathbf r(u,v)=\langle u + v, u - v, v\rangle
$$

for $0\le u\le 3$ and $0\le v\le 2$.

Use the formula

$$
\iint_S f\,\mathrm{d}S=\int_{0}^{2}\int_{0}^{3}f(\mathbf r(u,v))\|\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v\|\,\mathrm{d}u\,\mathrm{d}v.
$$

*Hint: The surface-area factor is $\|\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v\|=\sqrt{6}$. First substitute the coordinates into the scalar function and simplify.*
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a scalar surface integral, use

$$
\iint_S f\,\mathrm{d}S=\iint_D f(\mathbf r(u,v))\|\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v\|\,\mathrm{d}A.
$$

The supplied area factor is $\sqrt{6}$.

Substitute the coordinates and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}
f(\mathbf r(u,v))&=- \left(u + v\right) + \left(u - v\right) \\
&=- 2 v.
\end{aligned}
$$

Integrate over the parameter rectangle:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\iint_S f\,\mathrm{d}S&=\sqrt{6}\int_{0}^{2}\int_{0}^{3}\left(- 2 v\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\,\mathrm{d}v \\
&=\sqrt{6}\int_{0}^{2}\left[- 2 u v\right]_{u=0}^{u=3}\,\mathrm{d}v \\
&=\sqrt{6}\int_{0}^{2}\left(- 6 v\right)\,\mathrm{d}v \\
&=\sqrt{6}\left[- 3 v^{2}\right]_{v=0}^{v=2} \\
&=\sqrt{6}\left(\left(-12\right)-\left(0\right)\right) \\
&=- 12 \sqrt{6}.
\end{aligned}
$$

knowledge_point.title: Evaluating Surface Integrals Over Parametric Surfaces

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the surface integral

$$
\iint_S f(x,y,z)\,\mathrm{d}S,
$$

where $f(x,y,z)=x + y$ and

$$
\mathbf r(u,v)=\langle u + v, u - v, 2 v\rangle
$$

for $0\le u\le 3$ and $0\le v\le 1$.

Use the formula

$$
\iint_S f\,\mathrm{d}S=\int_{0}^{1}\int_{0}^{3}f(\mathbf r(u,v))\|\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v\|\,\mathrm{d}u\,\mathrm{d}v.
$$

*Hint: The surface-area factor is $\|\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v\|=2 \sqrt{3}$. First substitute the coordinates into the scalar function and simplify.*
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a scalar surface integral, use

$$
\iint_S f\,\mathrm{d}S=\iint_D f(\mathbf r(u,v))\|\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v\|\,\mathrm{d}A.
$$

The supplied area factor is $2 \sqrt{3}$.

Substitute the coordinates and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}
f(\mathbf r(u,v))&=\left(u + v\right) + \left(u - v\right) \\
&=2 u.
\end{aligned}
$$

Integrate over the parameter rectangle:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\iint_S f\,\mathrm{d}S&=2 \sqrt{3}\int_{0}^{1}\int_{0}^{3}\left(2 u\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\,\mathrm{d}v \\
&=2 \sqrt{3}\int_{0}^{1}\left[u^{2}\right]_{u=0}^{u=3}\,\mathrm{d}v \\
&=2 \sqrt{3}\int_{0}^{1}\left(9\right)\,\mathrm{d}v \\
&=2 \sqrt{3}\left[9 v\right]_{v=0}^{v=1} \\
&=2 \sqrt{3}\left(\left(9\right)-\left(0\right)\right) \\
&=18 \sqrt{3}.
\end{aligned}
$$
